method: Read the assigned ITEMs (PQ-09, PQ-10), the upstream shared/ guidance (anti_hallucination, evidence_contract, sink_definitions, php_specific_patterns) and the team4/skills config-auditor skills, then traced source->sink in the current working tree, including the vendor code the items point at (spatie/laravel-ignition 2.12.1, dcat/laravel-admin). No HTTP request, no payload and no container action was performed (MODE=static). .env values, secrets and password hashes are not reproduced; only non-secret boolean resolution facts are recorded.
environment_notes: Vendor versions resolved from vendor/composer/installed.json: spatie/laravel-ignition 2.12.1 (auto-discovered provider, extra.laravel.providers), league/flysystem 3.x LocalFilesystemAdapter + WhitespacePathNormalizer, dcat/laravel-admin as installed.
Working-tree .env exists (untracked, 0644) and resolves to APP_ENV=local and APP_DEBUG enabled; no IGNITION_* key is present. Values are deliberately not reproduced, only the resulting booleans.
Shipped template .env.example:2-4 is APP_ENV=production / APP_DEBUG=false, so the default deployment shape disables both endpoints under audit.
No php binary on the host, so nothing was executed. docker-compose stack was NOT touched.

The recon artifact docs/security-audit/raw/security-config.json already resolved the webdevops FPM bind question in an isolated container (host_runtime.commands[1]); this static pass re-derived the same conclusion from the repository's own build files without re-running the image.

findings.title: Ignition execute-solution / update-config are registered for every app and gated only by a runtime APP_DEBUG+APP_ENV check; in the current (local, debug-on) runtime an anonymous POST can run runnable solutions (APP_KEY rotation, migrate) and create .blade.php files
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / conditionally-exploitable (config-conditioned; current working-tree config satisfies the gate, shipped template does not)
findings.sink_type: privileged action execution behind a runtime-configuration guard (not RCE in this version; config-conditioned DoS/data-integrity)
findings.source: Anonymous HTTP request body of POST /_ignition/execute-solution: 'solution' (class name) and 'parameters' (array) -> ExecuteSolutionRequest::rules() (vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/Http/Requests/ExecuteSolutionRequest.php:12-18), read at ExecuteSolutionController.php:23-25. POST /_ignition/update-config reads theme/editor/hide_solutions (UpdateConfigRequest.php:12-16).
findings.sink: ExecuteSolutionController::__invoke() -> $solution->run($request->input('parameters', [])) (vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/Http/Controllers/ExecuteSolutionController.php:25), where the solution class is resolved from the request: SolutionProviderRepository::getSolutionForClass($this->input('solution')) -> class_exists()/class_implements()/app($solutionClass) (vendor/spatie/error-solutions/src/SolutionProviderRepository.php:71-86). Reachable runnable solutions in this install: GenerateAppKeySolution::run() -> Artisan::call('key:generate') (vendor/spatie/error-solutions/src/Solutions/Laravel/GenerateAppKeySolution.php:45-48) which rewrites APP_KEY with file_put_contents(environmentFilePath) (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Console/KeyGenerateCommand.php:95-115); RunMigrationsSolution::run() -> Artisan::call('migrate') (RunMigrationsSolution.php:101-104); MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution::run() -> file_put_contents($parameters['viewFile'], $output) (MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:78-84). UpdateConfigController -> IgnitionConfig::saveValues() -> FileConfigManager::writeToFile() -> file_put_contents($this->file, $content) (vendor/spatie/ignition/src/Config/FileConfigManager.php:140-147).
findings.reachability: The routes are registered unconditionally: IgnitionServiceProvider::boot() calls $this->registerRoutes() for every request (vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/IgnitionServiceProvider.php:61) and registerRoutes() only does loadRoutesFrom() (same file:211-214); the provider is auto-discovered (installed.json extra.laravel.providers) and Laravel's loadRoutesFrom() requires the file without adding the 'web' group, so the group carries only [RunnableSolutionsEnabled] and no CSRF/session middleware. Gate: RunnableSolutionsEnabled::handle() aborts 404 unless RunnableSolutionsGuard::check() (Http/Middleware/RunnableSolutionsEnabled.php:10-17). Guard order (Support/RunnableSolutionsGuard.php:13-36): (1) false when config('app.debug') is falsy; (2) if ignition.enable_runnable_solutions !== null return it; (3) false when app()->environment() is neither 'local' nor 'development'; (4) return config('app.debug'). Current working tree: config/app.php:44 'debug' => (bool) env('APP_DEBUG', false) resolves to enabled, .env APP_ENV resolves to a dev-like value, and ignition.enable_runnable_solutions is env('IGNITION_ENABLE_RUNNABLE_SOLUTIONS') (vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/config/ignition.php:160) which is unset -> null, so check() returns true and the endpoints answer. Shipped template .env.example:2-4 (APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false) makes step (1) return false -> 404. Route prefix is '_ignition' (config/ignition.php:198). The second controller-level check ensureLocalRequest() rejects only publicly routable request IPs (ExecuteSolutionController.php:38-51) while app/Http/Middleware/TrustProxies.php:19-35 leaves $proxies null by default (.env.example TRUSTED_PROXIES empty), so request()->ip() is the reverse-proxy/REMOTE_ADDR address (private docker network) and the check passes; update-config has no IP check at all.
findings.preconditions: 1) APP_DEBUG enabled AND APP_ENV in {local, development} (or IGNITION_ENABLE_RUNNABLE_SOLUTIONS=true) - true in the current working tree, false in the shipped .env.example. 2) The app publishes /_ignition/* through the front webserver (no separate deny rule exists in conf/default.conf or conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf; the only block is the PHP guard). 3) For key:generate to actually rewrite .env, APP_ENV must not be production (ConfirmableTrait) and /app/.env must be writable - docker-compose.yml:11 bind-mounts it read-write. 4) No authentication is required at any point.
findings.impact: Anonymous, unauthenticated state change/denial of service: rotate APP_KEY (invalidates all encrypted-at-rest payment credentials handled by the Pay model encrypted cast and logs out every admin/user session, with no recovery path for the previous key), run artisan migrate on a production DB, and create empty *.blade.php files anywhere the php-fpm user can write (absolute path accepted, but content is token-verified - see rejected items). update-config writes a JSON settings file for the php-fpm user. With APP_DEBUG=true the same runtime also renders Ignition stack traces containing environment values, so this item is a component of a broader debug-mode exposure. No remote code execution was found in ignition 2.12.1.

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/ignition-routes.php:9-20 (route group with only the RunnableSolutionsEnabled middleware), vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/config/ignition.php:160,198 (enable_runnable_solutions + housekeeping_endpoint_prefix '_ignition'), config/app.php:44 ('debug' => (bool) env('APP_DEBUG', false)), .env.example:2-4 (APP_ENV=production / APP_DEBUG=false).
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/Support/RunnableSolutionsGuard.php:13-36 (debug -> override -> environment -> debug), vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/Http/Middleware/RunnableSolutionsEnabled.php:10-17 (abort 404 when guard false), vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/IgnitionServiceProvider.php:61,211-214 (routes registered unconditionally, loadRoutesFrom adds no middleware group).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: POST /_ignition/execute-solution -> ExecuteSolutionController.php:25 -> GenerateAppKeySolution.php:45-48 (Artisan key:generate) / RunMigrationsSolution.php:101-104 (Artisan migrate) / MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:78-84 (file_put_contents); POST /_ignition/update-config -> UpdateConfigController.php:62-67 -> FileConfigManager.php:140-147.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: No CSRF: the route file is required outside the 'web' group (IgnitionServiceProvider.php:211-214), while the only CSRF middleware in the app is inside the 'web' group (app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43). No auth middleware on the group. Global stack app/Http/Kernel.php:19-26 does not block it (DujiaoSystem.php:17-30 only rewrites admin https config). No nginx deny for /_ignition in conf/default.conf:1-66 or conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:1-33.
evidence.EVID_CMD_EXEC_POINT: Indirect command execution: Artisan::call('key:generate') at GenerateAppKeySolution.php:47 and Artisan::call('migrate') at RunMigrationsSolution.php:103 - no shell string is built from user input, so no OS command injection, but a privileged console command is triggered by an anonymous HTTP request.
evidence.EVID_WRITE_CALLSITE: FileConfigManager.php:121,146 (file_put_contents of the settings file) and MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:82 (file_put_contents of the blade file).
evidence.EVID_WRITE_DESTPATH_RESOLVED: Settings file path = HOME/.ignition.json resolved from $_SERVER['HOMEDRIVE'].$_SERVER['HOMEPATH'] or getenv('HOME') (FileConfigManager.php:52-68,10); blade destination = $parameters['viewFile'] gated by isSafePath() requiring a '/' or './' prefix and a '.blade.php' suffix (MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:86-96).
evidence.EVID_WRITE_CONTENT_SOURCE: Settings file content = json_encode($request->validated()) with only theme|editor|hide_solutions (UpdateConfigRequest.php:12-16); blade content = original file content with " ?? ''" inserted after a chosen variable, verified by token comparison (MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:103-122).

findings.why_it_may_not_be_a_vulnerability: Static/constant and unreachable parts were rejected: (a) the two endpoints are 404 in the shipped configuration (.env.example APP_ENV=production / APP_DEBUG=false -> RunnableSolutionsGuard.php:13-16), and the docker deployment mounts an operator-supplied .env (docker-compose.yml:11), so production installs following the documentation are not exposed; (b) the reflex 'Ignition = CVE-2021-3129 RCE' mapping does not apply to 2.12.1 - MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution is path-allowlisted and token-verified, so no arbitrary content and no php://filter write was found; (c) update-config only persists three validated keys, so 'arbitrary config write' overstates it; (d) reaching the code still requires a deployment that runs with debug enabled, which is a configuration defect rather than a code defect. Because MODE=static and the deployment .env is operator-controlled, the verdict stays 'suspected' rather than 'confirmed'.
findings.remediation: Force-run production posture in the container (APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false) and add an explicit nginx deny for /_ignition/ in conf/default.conf and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf (defence in depth, so a debug flip does not expose the endpoints). Add IGNITION_ENABLE_RUNNABLE_SOLUTIONS=false to .env.example so the override branch (RunnableSolutionsGuard.php:22-26) fails closed instead of inheriting debug. Document in docs/php83-upgrade-deployment.md that debug mode must never be enabled on a reachable deployment because APP_KEY rotation (and stack-trace leakage) follows immediately.

findings.title: dcat-admin upload endpoints write to public/uploads with a client-supplied extension and no allow-list; PHP execution of those files is prevented only by the nginx location blocks, and SVG/HTML uploads are a same-origin stored-content primitive from the admin context
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / conditionally-exploitable (requires an authenticated administrator; the execution leg depends entirely on webserver configuration outside PHP)
findings.sink_type: file upload -> arbitrary-extension write into a web-served directory -> stored XSS; webshell only if the nginx deny rules are absent/overridden
findings.source: Admin-authenticated multipart POST: (a) /admin/dcat-api/tinymce/upload with 'file', 'dir', 'disk'; (b) /admin/dcat-api/editor-md/upload with 'editormd-image-file', 'dir', 'disk'; (c) /admin/dcat-api/form/upload with '_column' + file. Routes registered at vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:614-633 with middleware config('admin.route.middleware') and prefix admin_base_path('dcat-api') (Admin.php:616-621).
findings.sink: TinymceController::upload(): $newName = uniqid(md5($file->getClientOriginalName())).'.'.$file->getClientOriginalExtension(); $disk->putFileAs($dir, $file, $newName) (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Controllers/TinymceController.php:12-28); identical logic in EditorMDController.php:12-28. Disk name is taken from the request: request()->get('disk') ?: config('admin.upload.disk') (TinymceController.php:35, EditorMDController.php:35) and the directory from request()->get('dir') (line 15 / line 54). Target disk 'admin' -> 'root' => public_path('uploads'), 'url' => APP_URL/uploads (config/filesystems.php:72-77) with image/files subdirectories (config/admin.php:262-272).
findings.reachability: config/admin.php:74 sets the admin middleware chain ['web','admin','admin.force-password']; 'admin' expands to admin.auth, admin.pjax, admin.bootstrap, admin.permission, admin.session (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/AdminServiceProvider.php:80-85). Authentication is therefore required: Dcat\Admin\Http\Middleware\Permission::handle() lets the request through only for a logged-in user and short-circuits the permission check for isAdministrator() (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Middleware/Permission.php:27-40), and app/Http/Middleware/ForceAdminPasswordChange.php:32-45 only blocks when password_verify('admin', ...) matches. CSRF does apply ('web' group, app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43, and VerifyCsrfToken.php has no admin exception), so no cross-site upload. The extension surface /admin/auth/extensions (POST -> ExtensionController::store) is registered at Admin.php:594 but only runs Helper::validateExtensionName() regex ^[\w\-_]+/[\w\-_]+$ (Helper.php:527-530) before Artisan::call('admin:ext-make') (ExtensionController.php:127-140) - it scaffolds files, it does not accept attacker content.
findings.preconditions: 1) A valid admin session (the code itself assumes the shipped default password may be the literal 'admin', app/Http/Middleware/ForceAdminPasswordChange.php:36, and recon CFG-003 records that a fixed bcrypt administrator row ships in database/sql/install.sql). 2) For the execution leg: the /uploads/ (or /storage/) deny rules must be absent or the request must bypass nginx - i.e. an operator uses conf/default.conf without the ^~ block, an Apache/php artisan serve deployment, or a custom reverse proxy. 3) public/uploads must be writable by php-fpm (it is: Dockerfile:22-28, docker-compose.yml:15).
findings.impact: Any administrator (or anyone who obtains an admin session) can place files of arbitrary type and arbitrary content into the storefront origin: an .svg or .html payload executes script in the application origin, reaching other admins and storefront users (session/token theft, admin-action forgery) - this works even with the nginx deny rules in place, because only \.php$ and dotfiles are denied, not HTML/SVG. The same request stores a working .php webshell if the deny rules are missing or bypassed, which converts an admin session into RCE. Note also that the shipped image makes the app tree root-owned (Dockerfile:22-28) so a webshell under /uploads is the only write target the php-fpm user actually has.

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: config/admin.php:262-272 ('upload' disk 'admin', directories images/files), config/filesystems.php:72-77 (admin disk root public_path('uploads'), visibility public), config/admin.php:74 (admin route middleware chain).
evidence.EVID_WRITE_CALLSITE: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Controllers/TinymceController.php:20 and EditorMDController.php:20 ($disk->putFileAs($dir, $file, $newName)); UploadField.php:181-221 ($this->getStorage()->putFileAs($this->getDirectory(), $file, $this->name)) for the form upload path.
evidence.EVID_WRITE_DESTPATH_RESOLVED: Name = uniqid(md5(originalName)) . '.' . $file->getClientOriginalExtension() (TinymceController.php:25-28, EditorMDController.php:25-28, UploadField.php:313-316), so the extension is client-controlled; the directory is client-controlled via 'dir' (TinymceController.php:15) and is normalised, not escaped, by league/flysystem: Filesystem::writeStream() applies WhitespacePathNormalizer (vendor/league/flysystem/src/Filesystem.php:62-72) which throws PathTraversalDetected as soon as '..' would leave the disk root (vendor/league/flysystem/src/WhitespacePathNormalizer.php:33-51). Final location therefore always resolves inside public/uploads (or inside whichever configured disk is named in 'disk').
evidence.EVID_WRITE_CONTENT_SOURCE: Raw uploaded stream: putFileAs() streams $file->getRealPath() (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Filesystem/FilesystemAdapter.php:472-492); no mime/extension/content inspection is performed by either controller.
evidence.EVID_WRITE_EXEC_ACCESSIBILITY: Files under public/uploads are served directly by nginx: location ^~ /uploads/ { location ~ \.php$ { deny all; } try_files $uri =404; } (conf/default.conf:26-34 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:10-19), same for /storage/ (conf/default.conf:37-45). Nothing else prevents execution: cgi.fix_pathinfo=0 (conf/php.ini) and the FastCGI block is a plain regex location (conf/default.conf:57-65), so the only control is the webserver config. Dockerfile:19 installs conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf into webdevops vhost.common.d; Dockerfile-ARM64:21 installs conf/default.conf.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: No server-side allow-list exists: Image fields carry ['nullable','image'] (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Form/Field/Image.php:52) but the tinymce/editor-md controllers validate nothing, and UploadField::getValidationErrors() returns false (i.e. no validation) when the field defines no rules (UploadField.php:343-354).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Storefront origin APP_URL/uploads and APP_URL/storage (config/filesystems.php:72-77); the same origin serves the admin panel, so stored script content can act with admin cookies.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_a_vulnerability: Two of the item's three prongs do not hold and are listed in `rejected`: the published 9000:9000 port does not expose FPM (both build paths bind loopback), and 'dir'/'disk' cannot be used for path traversal (Flysystem normalisation). The remaining prong is a genuine defence-in-depth defect but is gated by administrator authentication - an administrator already controls goods, payment credentials and settings, so the added capability is stored same-origin script content (a real XSS primitive against other admins/storefront users) plus a webshell only in deployments that drop the nginx rules. That is why the item stays 'medium/suspected' and not 'high/confirmed'.
findings.remediation: Validate server-side instead of relying on the webserver: add an explicit extension/MIME allow-list for the tinymce, editor-md and form upload endpoints (or override the two controllers in app/Admin), reject svg/html/php/phar and double extensions, and force a generated extension from the detected MIME type instead of getClientOriginalExtension(). Keep the nginx ^~ /uploads/ deny blocks (they are the only execution barrier today), serve /uploads/ with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff plus a Content-Disposition for non-image types, and consider a separate cookie-less origin. Also drop the 9000:9000 publication from docker-compose.yml so a future pool-config change cannot expose FPM.

rejected.title: RCE via POST /_ignition/execute-solution + solution=MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution (CVE-2021-3129 style arbitrary file write / php://filter)
rejected.reason: The installed version cannot be abused that way. vendor/spatie/error-solutions/src/Solutions/Laravel/MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution.php:86-96 isSafePath() requires the path to start with '/' or './' AND to end with '.blade.php' (so 'php://filter/...', 'phar://...', 'data://...' and plain '.php' targets are refused), and makeOptional() at :103-122 re-tokenises the original and the modified Blade source and returns false unless the diff is exactly the inserted " ?? ''" after the requested variable - so the written content is never attacker-controlled. isRunnable() (:68-71) and run() (:78-84) both go through makeOptional(). Residual, non-RCE behaviour: an existing-but-empty read on a non-existent absolute path yields an empty file with a .blade.php suffix (file_get_contents false -> '' -> str_replace '' -> tokens [] on both sides -> file_put_contents writes ''). That is an empty-file creation primitive, not code execution, and it does not reach a web-served PHP path because the suffix must be .blade.php. Verdict: false positive for RCE.

rejected.title: POST /_ignition/update-config performs an 'arbitrary config write'
rejected.reason: UpdateConfigRequest::rules() (vendor/spatie/laravel-ignition/src/Http/Requests/UpdateConfigRequest.php:12-16) validates exactly three keys - theme (must be in [light, dark, auto]), editor (required string) and hide_solutions (required boolean) - and UpdateConfigController passes only $request->validated() to IgnitionConfig::saveValues() (UpdateConfigController.php:62-67). FileConfigManager then json_encodes that array into HOME/.ignition.json (FileConfigManager.php:129-147), so no PHP/config file is written and no code is injectable through 'editor'; additionally createFile()/writeToFile() return false unless the home directory and file are writable (FileConfigManager.php:42-45,111-122), which is often false under the shipped image user. Verdict: impact is a settings-file write for the php-fpm user, not an arbitrary configuration write.

rejected.title: docker-compose.yml:8 publishes 9000:9000 and conf/fpm-pool.conf:8 binds 127.0.0.1, therefore a reachable FPM bypasses the nginx /uploads deny rules
rejected.reason: Refuted on both build paths. (a) docker-compose.yml:4 builds the Dockerfile, which is webdevops/php-nginx:8.3 (Dockerfile:1) and only overrides conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf and conf/php.ini (Dockerfile:19-20); conf/fpm-pool.conf is never copied, so the effective pool is the image default, which recon verified listens on the loopback (docs/security-audit/raw/security-config.json host_runtime.commands[1], finding CFG-011: 'image pool listens on 127.0.0.1:9000, verified in webdevops/php-nginx:8.3'). (b) The ARM64 path does install conf/fpm-pool.conf (Dockerfile-ARM64:22) but that file sets listen = 127.0.0.1:9000 (conf/fpm-pool.conf:8), and docker-compose.arm64.yml:8-9 publishes only 80. A published port with no listener on a non-loopback address is not reachable, so no request can reach FPM from outside the container and the nginx deny rules cannot be bypassed this way. Residual (already recorded as CFG-011): the mapping is pointless and becomes dangerous if an operator changes the pool to 0.0.0.0 - a hardening issue, not a current finding. [Needs Verification] would require inspecting the built image's /opt/docker/etc/php/fpm/pool.d/, which is out of scope for MODE=static and was already done by recon.

rejected.title: Request-controlled 'dir' parameter on the dcat upload endpoints allows path traversal and writing a webshell outside public/uploads
rejected.reason: The traversal does not survive Flysystem. TinymceController.php:15 / EditorMDController.php:15 pass trim($request->get('dir'),'/') into FilesystemAdapter::putFileAs(), which calls $this->put($path.'/'.$name) (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Filesystem/FilesystemAdapter.php:483-485) -> Filesystem::writeStream(), which normalises the path with WhitespacePathNormalizer before hitting the local adapter (vendor/league/flysystem/src/Filesystem.php:62-72). WhitespacePathNormalizer::normalizePath() throws PathTraversalDetected as soon as a '..' segment appears with nothing left to pop (vendor/league/flysystem/src/WhitespacePathNormalizer.php:33-51), so 'dir=images/../../x', 'dir=../x' and absolute paths all collapse or throw and the write always lands inside the configured disk root. Combined with the item's own disk root (public/uploads) this is not an escape. Verdict: false positive for traversal/webshell-outside-uploads; the arbitrary-extension issue inside the root is covered by CFGSC-10.

rejected.title: /admin/auth/extensions (extension install) gives an authenticated admin arbitrary PHP code installation, therefore stored XSS/RCE
rejected.reason: The route exists (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:594, POST -> ExtensionController::store) but its write path is not attacker-content: ExtensionController::form() validates the package name with Helper::validateExtensionName(), regex ^[\w\-_]+/[\w\-_]+$ (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Support/Helper.php:527-530), and only then runs Artisan::call('admin:ext-make', ...) (ExtensionController.php:127-140), which generates stub code from that validated name. The InstallFromLocal zip path (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Forms/InstallFromLocal.php:15-76) extracts into config('admin.extension.dir') = base_path('dcat-admin-extensions') (config/admin.php:362-366), which the shipped images leave root-owned and non-writable for the php-fpm user (Dockerfile:22-28 chowns only storage, bootstrap/cache and public/uploads), so extraction fails with a permissions error rather than dropping executable code. It remains an intended admin-only extension feature (and becomes RCE if an operator chmods that directory) - reported as context for CFGSC-10, not as an independent finding.
